rationale: Targeted re-check of the 7 prior blocking findings: all 7 resolved on current source (RecursionError in _parse_filters now returns 422, page/per_page capped with over-limit tests, a real-engine test pins that a scope key in filters is ignored, and the 4 Types And Imports violations are fixed). business_review and standards_review are carried forward from the final round, so its code-quality row still reads partial although the violations behind it are resolved; the 2 deferred items (DF-001, DF-002) were not re-checked and remain in code-review-deferred.local.md.

findings.title: Nested filters JSON escapes as 500
findings.problem: _parse_filters catches only json.JSONDecodeError. A deeply nested `filters` payload (for example 1,000+ `[` characters) makes json.loads raise RecursionError, which escapes the handler uncaught.
findings.impact: GET /v1/settings answers this malformed input with a 500 instead of the documented 422 "Invalid filters". Reachability unconfirmed: it depends on the server's request-line limit admitting nesting past the interpreter's recursion limit.
findings.recommendation: In _parse_filters, add an `except RecursionError` branch next to `except json.JSONDecodeError` that raises the same 422 "Invalid filters" ExtendedHTTPException with a fixed details message (RecursionError has no `.msg`), and add a router test with deeply nested `filters`.
findings.check_notes: _parse_filters catches RecursionError and raises the 422 Invalid filters exception; test_bad_filters_return_422 adds a 20,000-level deep-nesting case.

fix.change: _parse_filters catches RecursionError and raises the same 422 Invalid filters ExtendedHTTPException with a fixed details message

findings.title: index_settings lacks return type annotation
findings.problem: code-quality.md Types And Imports says to avoid untyped public functions in new code and prefer explicit parameter and return types; the new public route handler index_settings has no return annotation.
findings.impact: A documented code-quality rule is broken in new code in this change; the Ruff configuration selects no annotation rules, so no automated gate catches it.
findings.recommendation: Annotate the return type of index_settings, e.g. `-> dict[str, Any]`, matching what SettingsIndexService.list_scopes returns.
findings.check_notes: index_settings is annotated -> dict[str, Any]; response_model=None keeps the OpenAPI shape unchanged.

fix.change: index_settings annotated -> dict[str, Any]; response_model=None keeps FastAPI from deriving a response model, so serialization and the OpenAPI response schema are unchanged
fix.test: tests/codemie/rest_api/router_guards/ (OpenAPI baseline shows no response-schema change)

findings.title: Optional[str] used instead of str | None
findings.problem: code-quality.md Types And Imports says to avoid `typing.Optional[X]` and prefer `X | None`; the new GET /v1/settings parameter is declared `filters: Optional[str] = None`, and Optional was newly added to the typing import at line 20 for it, while _parse_filters in the same file uses `str | None`.
findings.impact: A documented code-quality rule is broken in new code in this change; the Ruff configuration selects no pyupgrade rules, so no automated gate catches it.
findings.recommendation: Declare `filters: str | None = None` and drop Optional from the typing import at line 20.
findings.check_notes: filters is declared str | None = None; the typing import is now Any only.

fix.change: filters declared str | None = None; Optional dropped from the typing import

findings.title: Paging params on /v1/settings unbounded
findings.problem: The new route bounds `page` only with ge=0 and `per_page` only with ge=1. per_page=1000000 loads and masks every visible row in one request, and page=10**18 with per_page=10 produces an OFFSET (page * per_page, unclamped in _query_postgres) beyond PostgreSQL's bigint range.
findings.impact: An authenticated caller can pull an unbounded result set in one request (every project row for a platform admin), and an oversized page surfaces as a database error and 500 instead of a 422 on the new public endpoint; other paged routers in the codebase cap per_page at 100.
findings.recommendation: Add upper bounds following the project convention: `per_page: int = Query(10, ge=1, le=100)` (as in routers/skill.py:213 and routers/projects/crud.py:232) and an `le=` on `page` that keeps `page * per_page` inside PostgreSQL's bigint OFFSET range; extend test_bad_paging_returns_422 with over-limit cases and update the endpoint docstring's Paging section.
findings.check_notes: page le=MAX_PAGE ((2**63-1)//100) and per_page le=100; over-limit and boundary router tests added; docstring Paging section updated.

fix.change: per_page bounded le=MAX_PER_PAGE (100), page bounded le=MAX_PAGE ((2**63-1)//100) so page*per_page fits PostgreSQL bigint OFFSET; docstring Paging section and openapi.json baseline updated

findings.title: list_scopes signature uses Optional and bare dict
findings.problem: code-quality.md Types And Imports says to avoid `typing.Optional[X]` and bare `list`/`dict` annotations and prefer `X | None` with parameterized generics; the new list_scopes declares `filters: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None` and returns a bare `-> dict`.
findings.impact: A documented code-quality rule is broken in new code in this change; the Ruff configuration selects no pyupgrade or annotation rules, so no automated gate catches it.
findings.recommendation: Declare `filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None` and `-> dict[str, Any]` on list_scopes.
findings.check_notes: list_scopes declares filters: dict[str, Any] | None and returns -> dict[str, Any].

fix.change: list_scopes declares filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None and returns dict[str, Any]

findings.title: Scope-in-filters contract tested only against mock
findings.problem: The endpoint documents that a `scope` key inside `filters` is ignored, but test_scope_inside_filters_is_ignored patches SettingsIndexService.list_scopes and only asserts the forwarded kwargs. No real-engine test passes a `scope` key (the filter parametrization covers only search, project, type, is_global, created_by), so the contract rests untested on the generic unknown-key skip in BaseFilterData.add_sql_filters (broken-verification-gap; verified by reading the test and the filter class).
findings.impact: Clients of GET /v1/settings that send `filters` containing `scope`: if `scope` were added to SettingsFilter.FILTER_CONFIG or unknown keys started being rejected, the response would silently narrow to one scope or fail, and the existing test would still pass.
findings.recommendation: Add a real-engine case in tests/codemie/service/settings/test_settings_visibility_real_engine.py asserting that `SettingsIndexService.list_scopes(user=platform_admin, scopes=ALL, filters={"scope": "user"})` returns the same ids as the call without filters (PROJECT rows still present), or add `{"scope": "user"}` to the parametrized filters of test_list_scopes_all_filters_are_union_of_scopes with that check.
findings.check_notes: Real-engine test_list_scopes_all_ignores_scope_key_in_filters asserts filters={"scope": "user"} returns the unfiltered ids, Project rows included.

fix.change: Real-engine test asserts a scope key inside filters leaves the Scope All result unchanged, Project rows included

findings.title: New test modules omit future annotations import
findings.problem: code-quality.md Types And Imports says to add `from __future__ import annotations` in new modules; both modules this change adds, tests/codemie/rest_api/routers/test_settings_list.py and tests/codemie/service/settings/test_settings_visibility_real_engine.py, omit it.
findings.impact: A documented code-quality rule for new modules is not met by the two modules this change adds; no automated gate enforces it.
findings.recommendation: Add `from __future__ import annotations` after the license header in tests/codemie/rest_api/routers/test_settings_list.py and tests/codemie/service/settings/test_settings_visibility_real_engine.py.
findings.check_notes: Both new test modules now import from __future__ import annotations after the module docstring.

fix.change: from __future__ import annotations added to both new test modules

deferred.title: Wrong-typed filter values raise 500
deferred.problem: SettingsFilter compose functions accept untyped values, so e.g. {"search": 123} reaches escape_like_wildcards (expects str) and surfaces as a 500 rather than a 422; GET /v1/settings inherits this.
deferred.preexisting: Shared filter layer; /v1/settings/user and /project pass json.loads output to the same SettingsFilter unchanged today.

deferred.title: Unescaped _ in internal-alias LIKE
deferred.problem: alias.like("__internal__%") treats each _ as a wildcard, so a user's own alias such as "myinternal-x" is hidden from their list.
deferred.preexisting: Identical clause in the pre-change _query_postgres; spec requires visibility rules unchanged and the new test pins it (u_wild).

final_round.rationale: All four lenses and the standards audit ran against the spec and story (43/43 criteria pass); 7 major blockers remain: unbounded page/per_page on GET /v1/settings, an uncaught RecursionError in _parse_filters (reachability unconfirmed), a scope-in-filters contract tested only against a mock, and 4 code-quality Types And Imports violations. 2 deferred as pre-existing to code-review-deferred.local.md in the run dir: untyped filter values 500 in the shared SettingsFilter layer; unescaped `_` in the __internal__ LIKE hides matching user aliases. 11 lens candidates dismissed as already handled, spec-sanctioned or below the emission floor.
